content.problemStatement:
With a 32-bit integer `num`, output *a string representing its hexadecimal representation*. For negative integers, [two’s complement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two%27s_complement) method is used.

All the letters in the answer string should be lowercase characters, and there should not be any leading zeros in the answer except for the zero itself.

**Note:**You are not allowed to use any built-in library method to directly solve this problem.

**Example 1:**

```
Input: num = 26
Output: "1a"
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: num = -1
Output: "ffffffff"
```

**Constraints:**

* `-2^31 <= num <= 10^10 - 1`

notes: No built-in hexadecimal conversion is used.
Negative inputs are interpreted using their 32-bit two’s-complement bit pattern.
solution.approach: Treat the signed input as a 32-bit bit pattern. Repeatedly take the lowest 4 bits with num & 0xf, map 0-15 to 0-9/a-f, and shift right by 4. For negative inputs, first view the value as an unsigned 32-bit integer (num & 0xffffffff); this makes the two’s-complement representation explicit and guarantees termination. Reverse the collected digits and omit leading zeros; zero is the special case "0".

better.complexity: Time O(1), auxiliary space O(1) excluding the returned string.
better.description: Extract each hexadecimal digit directly from the low four bits with num & 0xf and shift right by four bits. This avoids division and naturally matches the hexadecimal/nibble representation; negative values are first masked to 32 bits.

optimal.complexity: Time O(1), auxiliary space O(1) excluding the returned string.
optimal.description: Convert negative inputs to their unsigned 32-bit representation, then process at most eight nibbles. Stop when a positive value becomes zero, reverse the digits, and return "0" for input zero. The fixed-width 32-bit representation makes both time and auxiliary space constant.

bruteForce.complexity: Time O(1), auxiliary space O(1) excluding the returned string.
bruteForce.description: Use repeated division by 16 and remainder extraction, with a 32-bit unsigned view for negative values. Map each remainder to a hexadecimal character and reverse the digits at the end. Because there are at most 8 hex digits, this is bounded by a constant number of steps.

solution.timeComplexity: O(1) because a 32-bit integer has at most 8 hexadecimal digits.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space; at most 8 output digits are stored.
